tools.name: telegram_get_me
tools.description: Return the bot's own profile (id, name, username, group-join and inline settings). Use it to confirm the token works. Bot API: getMe.

tools.name: telegram_get_chat
tools.description: Get the details of a chat the bot belongs to: type, title, username, description, pinned message, permissions. Bot API: getChat.

tools.name: telegram_get_chat_member_count
tools.description: Get the number of members in a chat. Bot API: getChatMemberCount.

tools.name: telegram_get_chat_member
tools.description: Get one member of a chat: status (creator, administrator, member, restricted, left, kicked) and rights. Bot API: getChatMember.

tools.name: telegram_get_chat_administrators
tools.description: List the administrators of a group or channel (not other bots' hidden admins). Bot API: getChatAdministrators.

tools.name: telegram_get_updates
tools.description: Read the messages and events that users sent to the bot and that wait in Telegram's queue (short poll, no wait). Without offset the same updates return again. A positive offset above an update_id, or a negative offset, deletes older updates in Telegram (this cannot be undone). allowed_updates change

tools.name: telegram_send_message
tools.description: WRITE: send a text message from the bot to a chat. The message is visible to real people and cannot be unsent except with telegram_delete_message. Bot API: sendMessage.

tools.name: telegram_edit_message_text
tools.description: WRITE: change the text of a message that the bot sent. This replaces the old text. Bot API: editMessageText.

tools.name: telegram_delete_message
tools.description: WRITE: delete a message. This cannot be undone. A bot can delete its own messages and incoming private-chat messages. In groups it needs the delete-messages admin right for other messages. Telegram allows deletion only for messages up to 48 hours old in most cases. Bot API: deleteMessage.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: telegram_get_chat, telegram_get_chat_member_count, telegram_get_chat_member, telegram_get_chat_administrators, telegram_get_updates · Private data: telegram_get_me, telegram_delete_message · Public sink: telegram_get_updates, telegram_send_message · Destructive: telegram_delete_message.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: telegram_get_chat, telegram_get_chat_member_count, telegram_get_chat_member, telegram_get_chat_administrators, telegram_get_updates · Private data: telegram_get_me, telegram_delete_message · Public sink: telegram_get_updates, telegram_send_message · Destructive: telegram_delete_message

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
